reviews.author: Johnny Williams
reviews.review_text: WARNING: Absolute scammers. Save your money and stay away. This auction is a complete rip-off designed to drain your wallet with hidden costs. The inspections are done by uncertified, untrained "technicians" who clear every single vehicle because the house only cares about collecting transaction fees. If you buy a vehicle that passes their garbage PSI and it breaks down immediately, their arbitration department completely ignores you. The person running arbitration is utterly clueless about cars and will leave you stuck with a lemon. Worse yet, their rules only work one way. If you sell a perfectly good vehicle, they will let the buyer return it for any minor excuse—even violating their own 14-day policy to hunt you down years later. To top it off, the front counter staff are incredibly corrupt. They intentionally slow down service to force new buyers into paying under-the-table bribes for basic assistance. Do not waste your time or risk your business here. Go to Manheim or Chicagoland instead.

reviews.source_label: Google Business Profile (America's Auto Auction Phoenix)
reviews.author: Vanessa Gutierrez
reviews.review_text: After paying our vehicle reinstatement and receiving confirmation from the lender, we called Dealers Auto Auction of the Southwest to schedule pickup. Having your vehicle repossessed is already a stressful and difficult situation. By the time customers are calling to arrange pickup, they have often worked incredibly hard to come up with the funds needed to reinstate their vehicle and get back to work and daily responsibilities. Instead of receiving clear information and professional assistance, we were met with an unhelpful attitude and were repeatedly told to listen to a voicemail. There was no empathy, patience, or understanding for the situation we were in. No one expects special treatment, but basic respect and professionalism should be the standard. In today’s economy, many hardworking people are one unexpected hardship away from finding themselves in a similar position. A little kindness goes a long way. I hope management takes customer service concerns seriously and provides additional training on how to communicate with people who are already dealing with difficult circumstances.

reviews.author: David
reviews.review_text: America’s Auto Auction should be ashamed of the way they handle vehicles, especially in situations where they’re dealing with repossessions. My experience with them was nothing short of a disaster, and their lack of professionalism, accountability, and basic respect for customers is appalling. After my vehicle was taken by White Sands Federal Credit Union (WSFCU) and sent to America’s Auto Auction, I went to retrieve it, only to find it in a completely trashed and damaged state. The inside was full of garbage, personal items were stolen—including valuable sunglasses, money, and sentimental objects, dash cameras, license plate, registration, etc.—and the vehicle itself had suffered significant physical damage inside and some out. This was not just negligence; this was outright vandalism. When I raised the issue with the staff at America’s Auto Auction, I was met with dismissive attitudes and zero accountability. They flat-out refused to take responsibility for the state my vehicle was in, despite the clear evidence that it had been mishandled while in their possession. They tried to shift blame to others, pointing fingers back at WSFCU,. They proceeded to show me pictures of my truck on intake which was already trashed and damaged and some of the pictures did not even match my interior or the vehicle, but the tech said that is what they uploaded and that was the answer I got. The worst part? They didn’t care. There was no attempt to make things right, no offer of compensation, and no effort to investigate or resolve the damage. I was left stuck with a trashed vehicle, stolen items, and a pile of repair costs, with America’s Auto Auction playing the role of the oblivious bystander, offering nothing but excuses. I did have a phone call from Melody and she said that one of the employees had trouble taking off the Dash cameras and that is why the rear view mirror was broken off...(first of all they had no right to be taking anything out of the truck). I had my days left. If you ever find yourself in a situation where America’s Auto Auction is involved, run the other way. They clearly don’t care about the people they affect or the property they mishandle. This is a business that operates with complete disregard for professionalism, customer service, and basic decency. Make things right America Auto! This is totally unethical and a shame you have employees that would do something like this.

reviews.author: Shawn
reviews.review_text: Serious post-sale issue regarding a Nissan Titan (that we purchased a post sale inspection on as well) purchased on September 18th and delivered to our store on September 19th following a Post Sale Inspection (PSI) on this specific unit. Upon delivery, our service department identified a faulty dosing valve, and we immediately scheduled service with Nissan. Nissan reprogrammed the dosing valve and returned the vehicle nearly a week later, stating the issue had been resolved. However, on the same day, the check-engine light reappeared. Nissan’s follow-up testing determined a #6 injector failure requiring replacement at a cost of approximately $4,000. Nissan further advised that the DEF malfunction and 5 mph speed restriction might persist even after the injector repair, and that the vehicle could additionally require complete catalytic converter replacements estimated at $9,887. Within two weeks of purchase, we contacted your auction regarding these concerns. We were informed that the vehicle was our responsibility and were offered four auction credits. The response we received from the manager (Rich Peyton) at that time was unsympathetic and dismissive of the seriousness of the issue, despite the scale of our partnership. While we understand occasional challenges in post-sale scenarios, the circumstances here, particularly with a vehicle that underwent your PSI, are unacceptable. Given the vehicle’s current state and the projected repair costs, we believe this transaction represents a complete breakdown of process and accountability. We are requesting that the vehicle be returned to your auction for unwind/repurchase.

reviews.review_text: The auction was well organized & punctual. They are very strict. Only licensed drivers can attend and participate in the auction. Everyone else has to wait in the lobby. They offer free coffee, cappuccino, donuts & fresh baked cookies. If you want to attend you must give the $1,000 to hold onto. If you win the bid on a car, the thousand goes toward the purchase price. You have until 4:00pm (I think that's the time they told us) to pay them the remainder of your winning bid. If you are not able to come up with the money in time, they keep the thousand. If you do not end up winning any bids or if you don't bid at all, you get your thousand back. Caution... There is a significant fee added onto the final bid price. My husband bid for a 2014 Jeep Compass North Limited. He won the bid at $1800. When he went to pay the remainder of what he owed for the vehicle, there was a $340 buyers fee (I think that's what they called it). So his $1800 Jeep was now $2140. Still, it was a steal! He did make the mistake of only looking at the drivers side of the car and didn't find out until it was time to drive the car off the lot that the passenger side must have been in a wreck because there were small dents on both doors and the front passenger window was (and still is) taped shut. Lesson learned! Even so, he still got a great deal on the Jeep. We will never buy a vehicle outside an auction again. I highly recommend it if you have the cash to participate.

reviews.review_text: I generally don't write reviews, but I feel compelled to share my experience given how long I've been purchasing cars from this place. Over the years, I've been a loyal customer, and during this time, I've consistently found the staff to be incredibly friendly and helpful. Everyone I've interacted with has been professional and courteous, which has made my car-buying experiences smooth and pleasant. I’ve never encountered any significant issues here, and that’s something I truly appreciate. However, there’s a recent change in their policy that I’m really not pleased with, and I think it’s important to mention. The new rule prohibits customers from opening the hoods of the cars to inspect the engines before placing a bid. This is something I find quite troubling, and I’m sure many other long-time customers feel the same way. When you’re in the market for a used car, being able to inspect the engine is a critical part of the process. It gives you a sense of the car's condition and helps you make an informed decision about whether or not to bid. Not being able to do so feels like a step backward in terms of transparency and customer service. I understand that policies evolve for various reasons, but this particular rule seems unfair and counterproductive. As someone who has been buying cars here for many years, I’m disappointed by this change. I hope the management reconsiders this decision, as it undermines the trust and confidence that customers have in making well-informed purchases. Until then, this rule will certainly affect how I approach future transactions here.

This auction is in the business of wiping their hands clean of as much responsibility as possible, taking the path of least resistance to correct wrongs, and rewarding the seller when they slip one through on a buyer. reviews.review_text: As a dealer I started buying cars here regularly. The office staff was always friendly and helpful. I simply asked for someone to file a police report for me with the local law enforcement and was told you would not even do that. I was looked straight in the face and told that there was absolutely nothing that you would do to help. I did not give anyone permission to leave our vehicles outside. A random transporter(that has never picked up cars for me there) called a cell phone of one of your employees with zero verification and they were left outside. If someone besides the owner of a vehicle calls my shop to have a car left outside of our fence with the keys in it, I am responsible if something happens to that vehicle. You know what the right thing to do is and you chose not to do it.
